subject: Use of survey sampling weights with SPDE in binomial likelihood models

messages.author: 7a0c0a1d5af6ca55
messages.subject: Use of survey sampling weights with SPDE in binomial likelihood models
parts:
Greetings all.

I am working with typical survey datasets (DHS specifically), where we have individual level observations (e.g. women/children), together with the village ID (cluster/primary sampling unit) they come from, each village has a longitude and latitude, the region (district/county) they come from, a sampling weight (inverse of inclusion probability - all women in a village have same sample weight), and a variable of interest (typically binary) e.g. a question on whether a woman uses modern contraceptive methods, so the dataset structure looks:

# A tibble: 27,565 × 6
   district  villageID.  longitude   latitude   weight       indicator
   <fct>      <dbl>       <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl>           <dbl+lbl>
 1 samburu  875      2121.          104.       0.244           1 [yes]  
 2 kajiado     1184     -416.           96.6      1.02              1 [yes]  
 3 laikipia    1069      1134.           95.8      0.717           0 [no]  
 4 kajiado     1190      -144.           102.       1.21            0 [no]  
 5 nairobi     1660      1101.           88.0      4.28            0 [no]

We are often interested in aggregating the data to the village level, or district level in order to compute the prevalence of the indicators, and make inference about the mean at the village of district level. For now I illustrate using the village level, and the two approaches that are commonly used: (NOTE: each village has a unique sampling weight, and a unique longitude and latitude for location)

First method: We incorporate the weighting into the number of trials and successes (caveat: since the weights are non-integer, we will have to round them off (or multiply by a scale and round-off )downstream so the they are integers, as binomial likelihood deals with strictly integer counts)

d1 <-  z |>
  group_by(villageID, district) |>
  reframe(
    success = sum(indicator * weight),
    trials = sum(weight)
  )

head:
  villageID district        success trials
      <dbl> <fct>             <dbl>  <dbl>
1       975 elgeyo.            3.67   7.80
2      1130 narok             14.8   28.4
3      1132 narok              5.01  10.6


Second method: We compute number of successes and trials by summing, and also retain the village sampling weight independently
d2 <- z |>
  group_by(villageID, district) |>
  reframe(trials = n(),
          success = sum(indicator),
          weight = unique(weight))

head:
villageID district        trials success weight
      <dbl> <fct>            <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>
1       975 elgeyo.              17       8     0.459
2      1130 narok               25      13     1.14
3      1132 narok               19       9      0.557

Fitting a model with these two datasets gives similar estimates to about 4 decimal places (especially for the coefficients and the predictions, the sd and confidence intervals are a bit different). I care mostly about the predicted mean estimates for the villages:

m1 <- inla(success ~ 1, data = d1 |> mutate(success = round(success, 0),
                                            trials = round(trials, 0)), family = "binomial", Ntrials = trials)

m2 <- inla(success ~ 1, data = d2, family = "binomial", Ntrials = trials, weights = weight)


The issue however arises, when we want to add an SPDE component to the model, as adding the SPDE leads to at times (almost similar predictions between the two models, with correlations of about 0.96 between their predictions and close values for the intercepts etc), but at times (for certain indicators), the values are worryingly different, and there are large deviations.



1. From a statistical viewpoint, what is the recommended aggregation procedure ?
2. For working with SPDE models with binomial likelihood, what should I know if I am to incorporate sampling weights as well ?
3. A tricky challenge for me is, what weights to use for pixels from the prediction grid, and so far my best bet is to assume a weight of 1 for all upsampled locations, when predicting to the rest of the upsampled pixels, (this is why I would wish to work with aggregation method 1, which omits the need for using weights downstream), is there any advice/best practise on this so far ?

I am able to supply datasets and codes for checking this.

Thanks in advance.

Thanks 
Indeed, I had already gone through the source codes for the SUMMER and surveyPrev package, and they only cover discrete spatial models (BYM2 / IID).
In the same, they ignore the sampling weights.

I will contact Jon Wakefield and team, and I will also be waiting to hear from anyone in this forum who has had any experience with weighted regression in the context of SPDE models.
